Exercise: Plank

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
static

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- static

Primary Muscles:

- abdominals

Secondary Muscles:
None

Equipment:

- bodyweight

Fatigue Score:
2

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
3

Energy Requirement:
low to moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- posture_improvement
- core_strength_and_stability

Contraindications:

- Individuals with lower back pain should perform this exercise with caution and may need to modify the position.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Plank with Arm Raise, force: static, level: intermediate, mechanic: isolation
- name: Plank with Leg Raise, force: static, level: intermediate, mechanic: isolation

Substitution Options:

- name: Side Plank, force: static, level: beginner, mechanic: isolation

Instructions:

- Get into a prone position on the floor, supporting your weight on your toes and your forearms. Your arms are bent and directly below the shoulder.
- Keep your body straight at all times, and hold this position as long as possible. To increase difficulty, an arm or leg can be raised.
